answer: In an agent economy each claimed identity must summit a unique computational island by deriving a private key from a zephyr-seeded random beacon and solving a memory-hard puzzle whose difficulty multiplies with simultaneous claims from the same hardware fingerprint. An attacker spinning up thousands of sybils faces quadratic growth in RAM and CPU time because the puzzles share no reusable work, forcing rental of ever-larger clusters while honest agents solve once and persist.
